subject: biology
topicDisplay: Theme B · Molecules & Cells (Carbs, Lipids, Proteins, Membranes, Organelles)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The monomer of starch is:
questions.explain: Starch is a polymer of alpha-glucose.

questions.q: Two monosaccharides join into a disaccharide by:
questions.explain: Condensation forms a glycosidic bond and releases water.

questions.q: An unsaturated fatty acid contains:
options: One or more C=C double bonds
questions.explain: Double bonds create kinks, lowering melting point.

questions.q: Lipids are used for long-term energy storage in animals because they:
options: Store about twice the energy per gram of carbohydrate
questions.explain: Being highly reduced and hydrophobic, lipids store much energy compactly.

questions.q: A phospholipid is amphipathic because it has:
options: A hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails
A charged tail and neutral head
questions.explain: This drives bilayer formation in water.

questions.q: Amino acids are joined by:
questions.explain: Peptide bonds form by condensation between amino acids.

questions.q: The primary structure of a protein is:
questions.explain: Primary structure determines all higher levels of folding.

questions.q: High temperature denatures an enzyme by:
options: Disrupting the bonds holding its tertiary structure
questions.explain: Denaturation changes the shape of the active site so substrate no longer fits.

questions.q: The full set of proteins made by a cell is its:
questions.explain: The proteome varies between cell types, unlike the fixed genome.

questions.q: The basic framework of a cell membrane is the:
questions.explain: Proteins are embedded in a fluid phospholipid bilayer (fluid mosaic model).

questions.q: Movement of oxygen down its gradient without proteins or ATP is:
questions.explain: Small nonpolar molecules diffuse directly through the bilayer.

questions.q: Active transport requires ATP because it moves substances:
questions.explain: Pumping from low to high concentration needs energy (e.g. the sodium–potassium pump).

questions.q: A red blood cell placed in distilled water will:
questions.explain: Water enters by osmosis; without a wall the cell can lyse.

questions.q: Uptake of large particles by the membrane folding inward is:
questions.explain: Endocytosis engulfs material into a vesicle; exocytosis releases it.

questions.q: The double membrane and cristae are features of the:
questions.explain: Cristae increase surface area for aerobic respiration.

questions.q: A benefit of compartmentalization by membranes is that it:
options: Allows different reactions in separate optimal environments
questions.explain: Organelles keep incompatible processes and optimal conditions apart.

questions.q: Secreted proteins are typically processed in the order:
questions.explain: Proteins made on the rough ER are modified by the Golgi and exported in vesicles.

questions.q: Cell specialization occurs because different cell types:
options: Express different subsets of the same genes
questions.explain: Differentiated cells share a genome but express different genes.

questions.q: A stem cell is a cell that can:
options: Divide and differentiate into other cell types
questions.explain: Stem cells self-renew and differentiate.

questions.q: The enucleate, biconcave shape of a red blood cell is an adaptation that:
options: Maximises space and surface area for oxygen transport
questions.explain: Loss of the nucleus creates room for haemoglobin and aids gas exchange.
